summary:
The common lizard (*Zootoca vivipara*) is a small Eurasian reptile notable for having the widest range of any lizard and reaching farther north than any other non-marine, non-avian reptile. It lives in habitats from grassland to woodland and survives cold climates by basking, hibernating, and, in extreme conditions, freezing and later thawing.

Most populations give birth to live young, but some in northern Spain and southwestern France lay eggs. The species is insectivorous and typically lives five to six years. Males have larger heads, which help them compete for mates. Females show inherited yellow, orange, or mixed coloration, and the different color types have distinct reproductive advantages.
